title: anchored-threshold-oscillation-notes-gz
content:
Purpose: personal scratchpad to capture a lightweight protocol for dealing with canary oscillation (traffic moving back and forth between control and new model) when we observe metric drift spikes. Goal is an operationally simple, observable, reversible set of anchors and damping steps that engineers can run without approval in low-severity cases and escalate when thresholds are exceeded.

Context / motivation:
- We've seen subtle oscillation patterns when small cohorts cause transient p95 spikes and the autoscaler + client-side retries cause amplification.
- Existing playbooks are either too coarse (full rollback) or too manual (hand-tune cohorts). Need deterministic anchors and a fast way to dampen oscillation.

High-level idea (one-liner):
- Anchor the new variant to a stable baseline fraction (anchor fraction) and apply a time-decayed damping multiplier to release growth. If oscillation persists, automatically freeze and warm a safety cohort before resuming.

Key terms (for this note):
- anchor_fraction: initial fixed fraction we pin new variant to (e.g., 0.05).
- oscillation_event: 5-min window where p95 increases > 40% vs baseline AND error_rate increases > 0.5pp.
- damping_multiplier: multiplier applied to any scheduled traffic increases (0.5 by default).
- freeze_window: how long to keep traffic pinned when oscillation detected (15m default).
- safety_warmup: small seeded cohort (0.01) sent to new variant with increased logging and KV priming.

Quick checklist (run when you see oscillation):
- [ ] Confirm metric sanity: check p50/p95/p99 + error rate + 95th token timeouts in telemetry.
- [ ] Determine whether oscillation is client-triggered (retries) or server-side (GPU saturation). Look at client retry spikes and per-host connect_count.
- [ ] Set anchor_fraction=0.05 and pin via routing API: PATCH /internal/routing {"route":"/v1/generate","variant":"v2.7","fraction":0.05,"pin":true} (example).
- [ ] Apply damping: reduce pending rollout increments by damping_multiplier=0.5.
- [ ] Start safety_warmup cohort (seeded 1% of anchor fraction) with heavy logging and model debug flags.
- [ ] Wait freeze_window (15m) and re-evaluate metrics.
- [ ] If stable -> unpin and resume slow ramp (max +1% per 30m). If not -> escalate to SRE and product owner.

Anchoring heuristics (measured values I want to try in next runs):
- anchor_fraction: 0.03 for high-latency models, 0.07 for low-latency; default 0.05.
- freeze_window: 15m (short outages), 60m (if p95>500ms and error rate >2%).
- damping_multiplier: 0.5 (gentle), 0.25 (aggressive).
- backoff schedule when oscillation repeats: 15m -> 30m -> 60m -> 3h.

Observability signals to watch (dashboard swarm):
- Latency: p50, p95, p99 (client and server side), token-level slowdowns.
- Errors: total 5xx, model-level errors, truncated_responses.
- Retries: client-side retry rate and retry-loop ratio (requests that retried >1).
- Capacity: GPU util, queue_depth, batch_size distribution.
- Freshness: KV-cache hit rate (cache churn can cause latency spikes).

Quick commands / snippets (ops):
- Pin route (curl):
  curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","variant":"v2.7","fraction":0.05,"pin":true}' https://api.redwood.local/internal/routing

- Start safety warmup via feature-flag rollout (example):
  ./scripts/rollout_seed --route "/v1/generate" --variant v2.7 --fraction 0.0005 --duration 30m --debug-logs

- Recompute baseline snapshot for comparison:
  python tools/snapshot_baseline.py --route "/v1/generate" --window 1h --out /tmp/baseline.json

Simulation notes (to-run before next Tuesday):
- Run the oscillation simulator with different client retry patterns to ensure our damping_multiplier prevents amplification.
- Command (local sim): ./tools/simulate_oscillation --model v2.7 --clients 5000 --retry-dist "heavy" --duration 2h --out /tmp/sim-v2.7.json
- Success criteria in sim: after an oscillation_event, pinned anchor + damping should return p95 to within 10% of baseline within two freeze windows.

Open questions / trade-offs (callouts for design doc):
- How much observability latency do we accept for automatic damping? If metrics are delayed >60s, oscillation may overshoot. Need to quantify metric ingestion lag.
- Should anchors be per-region or global? Probably per-region for region-specific saturation.
- How to handle multivariate failures (latency up, but generation_quality improves)? Need a decision matrix for quality vs latency tradeoffs.
- Should we automagically escalate to fallback model (smaller, cheaper) after N repeated oscillations? Proposal: after 3 oscillation cycles in 24h, route to v-compact fallback.

Escalation matrix (handy):
- tier 1 (owner can run): transient oscillation_event, no user-visible errors, p95 < 750ms -> run anchor/damping checklist.
- tier 2 (SRE + owner): persistent oscillation after 2 freeze_windows OR error_rate increase >1.5pp -> engage SRE, consider rollback or region diversion.
- tier 3 (oncall, exec): user-facing or revenue impact >1% conversions lost OR outage -> full incident.

Notes to self (personal reminders):
- Keep the anchor_fraction conservative for models that use long-lookback KV (they are pain to warm).
- When warming safety cohort, push priming requests that match typical long contexts to prefill KV. Document sequences we used for v2.6 warmups.
- Add a tiny feature to the console: quick "anchor" button that sets fraction and damping in one click + auto-checklist. Filing UX ticket later.

Immediate next actions (this week):
- [ ] Run a controlled sim with heavy client retries (assign Ravi).
- [ ] Draft a short ops-runbook from these notes and attach to JIRA-2145 (me).
- [ ] Prototype "anchor" button mock in Figma (María).

Slack crumbs: #deploys-alerts for quick broadcasts, #serving-runtime for SRE pings, tag @oncall when escalation needed.

Versioning note: keep this doc as scratch; if we standardize the protocol, move to shared_drives/engineering/release-engineering/anchored-threshold-protocol-v1.md

End of scratchpad.
summary: Personal scratchpad describing an anchoring + damping protocol for release oscillation, with checklist, heuristics, commands, simulation notes, and open questions.
